subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: Grouping: all nine step modules set groupKey: 'story' and Scene: StoryScene. Stage.tsx keys its motion.div with sceneKey(step). In steps.ts, sceneKey returns `group:${groupKey}:${sceneId}`, derived from groupKey and the Scene component identity, so all nine steps get the same key. The one mounted scene is updated with a new payload.stage instead of remounting. Identity: the presentation-owned ENTITIES in entities.ts carry fixed ids, and entitiesThrough only filters them cumulatively. Scene.tsx passes def.id as id (and as React key) to every kit node. The kit's useEntityProps in entity.ts sets layoutId: id, a layout transition, and data-presentation-entity. Box, SymbolChip, Arrow, Label, Emphasis and Frame all call it. Persisting ids therefore morph through motion layoutId. Every ENTITIES member is rendered through Entity, so none is dead, including the arrows 'conversation', 'verify-chain', 'modify-arc' and 'edit-link'. groupKey preserves the scene mount; the separate layoutId values preserve entity identity.

criteria.rationale: Every identity-bearing entity the sample renders goes through useEntityProps, which spreads useEntrance(id). A newcomer therefore gets initial opacity 0 and an opacity animation delayed by ENTER_DELAY (0.5 s) once the stage has started. That equals LAYOUT_T (0.5 s), the layout duration the continuing entities use. Continuing ids get initial:false and delay 0. The delay sits inside animate.transition, so it applies only to the opacity entry. The layout morph uses a separate transition.layout with duration LAYOUT_T and no delay, so the two are not both pushed late. The sample's Scene.tsx renders all entity kinds (node, card, ghost, tray, chip, arrow, label, check, flag, frame) through Box, SymbolChip, Arrow, Label and Emphasis, plus Frame. Each of these calls useEntityProps. The only other markup is the unidentified card-part spans inside a Box, which are structural wrappers and not entities. In the grouped scene the keyed Entity stays mounted across payload updates. useEntrance fixes its state on first mount, so continuing entities never replay the fade.

criteria.rationale: The suite that drives a browser is set in vitest.browser.config.ts (include 'tests/browser/**/*.test.ts'). That glob matches exactly three files: inspect.int.test.ts, verify.e2e.test.ts and bootstrap.int.test.ts. helpers.ts is their shared module. The unit config runs tests/unit under jsdom and does not drive a real browser. I quote all four browser files in full, and none of them sleeps for a fixed time or uses an immediately-returning call as a wait. (1) inspect.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits runNpm subprocess runs. The only direct Playwright test, 'captures only after the transition settles', awaits chromium.launch, page.setContent and page.evaluate, and the evaluate awaits img.decode(). It then asserts on pixel counts that have already been computed. The remaining tests assert on PNG files and output that the completed runs produced. (2) verify.e2e.test.ts: every test awaits runNpm and then asserts on the finished process's output and exit code. previewIsGone is a fetch bounded by AbortSignal.timeout. The only setTimeout in the file is in-page app code that a fault case injects into Scene.tsx. (3) bootstrap.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits spawnSync and runNpm, and the tests assert on their results and on file contents. (4) helpers.ts: runNpm resolves on the child's 'close' event. Its setTimeout is only a SIGKILL safeguard for a hung child, not a wait before an assertion. Inside the scripts, step changes are awaited by polling: waitForStepIndex calls page.waitForFunction on data-step-index with a timeout. Judge C's fail rests on page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) at scripts/lib/inspect-run.mjs:50. That call is in the delivered inspect helper, not in a test. The helper reaches it only after waitForStepIndex has confirmed the step (line 45), so the test's step assertions are not waiting on a sleep. The settle delay is a product option (--settle-ms) that the test exercises: it compares default-delay captures with --settle-ms 0 captures. The test does not use it to time its own assertions. The criterion is about how the browser tests wait, and the guidance excludes settle-delay length from scoring. Judge C's reason therefore does not decide the requirement, and I agree with Judges A and B.

votes.rationale: Talk.tsx renders the kit's Presentation with the STEPS array, title, className and initialMode, so the kit handles navigation, chrome and stage. The shared StoryScene is typed with the kit's SceneProps and wraps its content in SceneLayer. It builds every entity from the kit's Box, SymbolChip, Arrow, Label, Emphasis and Frame. The demo does not re-implement nav, fit-scale, stage or entrance logic. Stage.tsx calls the step's Scene with payload, step meta and index, which is the API StoryScene implements.

votes.rationale: Grouping: all nine step modules set groupKey: 'story' and Scene: StoryScene. Stage.tsx keys its motion.div with sceneKey(step). In steps.ts, sceneKey returns `group:${groupKey}:${sceneId}`, derived from groupKey and the Scene component identity, so all nine steps get the same key. The one mounted scene is updated with a new payload.stage instead of remounting. Identity: the presentation-owned ENTITIES in entities.ts carry fixed ids, and entitiesThrough only filters them cumulatively. Scene.tsx passes def.id as id (and as React key) to every kit node. The kit's useEntityProps in entity.ts sets layoutId: id, a layout transition, and data-presentation-entity. Box, SymbolChip, Arrow, Label, Emphasis and Frame all call it. Persisting ids therefore morph through motion layoutId. Every ENTITIES member is rendered through Entity, so none is dead, including the arrows 'conversation', 'verify-chain', 'modify-arc' and 'edit-link'. groupKey preserves the scene mount; the separate layoutId values preserve entity identity.

votes.rationale: The kit chrome emits semantic and stable hooks without styling. Toc entries and progress dots set aria-current='step' plus data-presentation-active='true' for the active item. Attribution.tsx is a project-local anchor whose default href and label come from the local constants.ts (ATTRIBUTION_URL, ATTRIBUTION_LABEL). The presentation-owned style.css makes the active state visibly distinct, with a wider accent-filled dot and an accent-tinted bold TOC entry with a left border. It also styles the attribution (muted color, 0.8rem, hover/focus accent). A grep of src/presentation-kit for color, background, font, border and hex or rgb values found no matches, so the kit carries no default colors, fonts, borders or theme tokens.

checks.rationale: I confirm the dissent. The supplied material shows what it claims, and the review guidance counts this case as a missing sample. The verifier does catch two kinds of missing sample correctly: - **Not registered:** `checkSample.registered` fails in the sample phase, before the preview starts. - **Wrong steps:** a wrong step count, or a wrong or out-of-order title, caption or era, fails in the sample phase. The gap is an empty step list. The guidance defines a missing sample to include steps content that is "absent". With no steps, `Presentation.tsx` returns null (`const step = steps[index]; if (!step) return null`), so the `data-step-count` hook never renders. In `renderPresentation`, the explicit count check (`checkSample.count`) comes after `page.waitForSelector('[data-step-count]', { timeout: STEP_TIMEOUT_MS * 2 })`. That wait times out first, and the run fails with `PhaseError('render', ... 'presentation did not render a step (no data-step-count hook)')`. So the empty-steps case never reaches a check that reports the sample as missing or not matching the outline. It surfaces only as a browser wait timeout labelled `[render]`, which the guidance says fails this criterion. The majority says this is a constructed deletion the guidance excludes. But the guidance excludes only partial deletions, such as removing an imported file while its import remains. It explicitly lists absent steps as a missing-sample case. The majority's reliance on the unregistered and out-of-order cases does not cover this branch.

The case 'an out-of-order sample fails naming the step' asserts a sample-phase failure at step 1 (index 0). Judges A and C reached the same conclusion. Judge B argues that an emptied step list would only fail as a render timeout. That scenario is a constructed deletion that the guidance tells reviewers not to build, and the candidate does not produce it. B also accepts that a missing registration is caught explicitly. The guidance's main missing-sample cases are an unregistered sample and an out-of-order outline, and both fail with a non-zero exit at a check that names the sample phase. result.rationale: The suite that drives a browser is set in vitest.browser.config.ts (include 'tests/browser/**/*.test.ts'). That glob matches exactly three files: inspect.int.test.ts, verify.e2e.test.ts and bootstrap.int.test.ts. helpers.ts is their shared module. The unit config runs tests/unit under jsdom and does not drive a real browser. I quote all four browser files in full, and none of them sleeps for a fixed time or uses an immediately-returning call as a wait. (1) inspect.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits runNpm subprocess runs. The only direct Playwright test, 'captures only after the transition settles', awaits chromium.launch, page.setContent and page.evaluate, and the evaluate awaits img.decode(). It then asserts on pixel counts that have already been computed. The remaining tests assert on PNG files and output that the completed runs produced. (2) verify.e2e.test.ts: every test awaits runNpm and then asserts on the finished process's output and exit code. previewIsGone is a fetch bounded by AbortSignal.timeout. The only setTimeout in the file is in-page app code that a fault case injects into Scene.tsx. (3) bootstrap.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits spawnSync and runNpm, and the tests assert on their results and on file contents. (4) helpers.ts: runNpm resolves on the child's 'close' event. Its setTimeout is only a SIGKILL safeguard for a hung child, not a wait before an assertion. Inside the scripts, step changes are awaited by polling: waitForStepIndex calls page.waitForFunction on data-step-index with a timeout. Judge C's fail rests on page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) at scripts/lib/inspect-run.mjs:50. That call is in the delivered inspect helper, not in a test. The helper reaches it only after waitForStepIndex has confirmed the step (line 45), so the test's step assertions are not waiting on a sleep. The settle delay is a product option (--settle-ms) that the test exercises: it compares default-delay captures with --settle-ms 0 captures. The test does not use it to time its own assertions. The criterion is about how the browser tests wait, and the guidance excludes settle-delay length from scoring. Judge C's reason therefore does not decide the requirement, and I agree with Judges A and B.

scene-kit.rationale: Newcomer entry is delayed by ENTER_DELAY (0.5 s), equal to LAYOUT_T (0.5 s). buildEntrance puts that delay only in animate.transition, which governs the opacity fade. useEntityProps sets a separate top-level transition.layout with duration LAYOUT_T and no delay, so the continuing entities' layout morph is not delayed. Continuing ids get initial:false and delay 0. The first scene also gets delay 0, because the stage has not started. After the first commit, Stage calls markStarted(), so later newcomers get the delay. Scene.tsx renders every identity-bearing entity kind (node, card, ghost, tray, chip, arrow, label, check, flag, frame) through Box, SymbolChip, Arrow, Label, Emphasis or Frame. Each of those calls useEntityProps, which spreads useEntrance. The only other markup is the unidentified card-part spans, which are structural. The grouped scene keeps keyed entities mounted, and useEntrance decides once per mount. stage.test.tsx also checks that a grouped newcomer starts at opacity 0 and that ENTER_DELAY >= LAYOUT_T.

scene-kit.rationale: Stage uses AnimatePresence with the default sync mode, not wait. The outgoing scene stays mounted, and its wrapper is position:absolute so it is out of layout flow. scene-kit.rationale: A newcomer's opacity animation is delayed by ENTER_DELAY = 0.5 s. That equals LAYOUT_T = 0.5 s, the layout duration continuing entities use. stage.test.tsx asserts ENTER_DELAY >= LAYOUT_T, the delay value, and that a grouped newcomer starts at opacity 0 while the continuing node is never hidden.

verification-tooling.rationale: startPreview takes an ephemeral port from freePort, which closes its probe server before the child is spawned. It then starts the child with --strictPort. The `exited` flag is checked only at the top of each loop iteration, before the fetch, and is never raced against it. A stale server on the port could answer before the child's exit is seen. engineering-quality.rationale: startPreview spawns vite's bin with process.execPath, so the child is the server itself and not an npm/npx wrapper. stop() sends SIGTERM, escalates to SIGKILL after 3s, and awaits the child's exit. The readiness-timeout path calls stop() before throwing. verify.mjs puts startPreview, chromium.launch and the checks in one try with `finally { browser?.close(); preview?.stop() }`. runInspect does the same. A browser launch failure, a failing check or a later error therefore all reach stop(). The bootstrap template copies are identical.

engineering-quality.rationale: The criterion fails only on four things: a relative import resolving outside src, an unresolved CSS import, a missing required kit prop, or a field name that doesn't match the kit's types. The supplied source shows none of them. SKILL.md documents the destination as `src/presentations/<slug>/`. From there, `../../presentation-kit` in Scene.tsx and Talk.tsx resolves to `src/presentation-kit`. `../../../presentation-kit` in steps/index.ts, step1.tsx and step2.tsx resolves to the same place. `../Scene` and `./entities` resolve to sibling files. Talk.tsx imports `./style.css`, the template ships that file, and tsconfig.app.json has `types: ["vite/client"]`, so the CSS import type-checks and resolves. Props match the kit types. Box, SymbolChip and Frame take id, x, y, w, h and className, and Frame's children are optional. Arrow takes id, from, to, bidirectional and className, and the template's `Point` is structurally identical to the kit's. Presentation takes steps and title, and passes className and initialMode. Step fields are id, era, title, caption, groupKey, Scene and payload, which match `Step<StoryPayload>`. `StoryScene` takes `SceneProps<StoryPayload>`, as the `Scene` field requires. Under strict, noUnusedLocals, verbatimModuleSyntax and erasableSyntaxOnly, the imports are all used and type-only imports carry `type`, and the switch over the discriminated union is exhaustive. The inspect templates are .mjs scripts outside `src`, so they are not type-checked or built. Their imports are sibling script paths, not paths into or out of src. Some of those sibling files (lib/preview.mjs, lib/diagnostics.mjs and others) are not in the packet. The criterion's clauses don't depend on them, and the contracts test asserts the template scripts match the repository's scripts. There is no materialize-and-build test, but the trace alone meets the criterion.

audit_results.rationale: The quoted lines meet the requirement as the review guidance defines it. A missing sample means the reference presentation is not registered, or its titles, captions or steps are missing or out of order. 1. **Unregistered sample.** In scripts/verify.mjs (lines 86-91), main() runs a 'sample' phase after the build and before the preview starts. It calls checkSample.registered for each expectation. scripts/lib/sample-check.mjs (lines 5-11) returns an explicit message when the slug is not registered or its title differs. main() throws that as PhaseError('sample'). 2. **Steps missing or out of order.** renderPresentation compares the reported step count with the expected count (verify.mjs lines 41-44, sample-check.mjs lines 13-16). A missing or non-numeric step count becomes 0 or NaN, which never equals the expected count, so it cannot pass. For each step, the era, title and caption are compared with the expected values for that index (verify.mjs lines 58-65, sample-check.mjs lines 18-27). Each mismatch throws PhaseError('sample') and names the step. 3. **Exit code and output.** The top-level handler prints 'FAIL verify [sample]: …' and calls process.exit(1) (verify.mjs lines 111-117). That is a non-zero exit whose output names the failed phase. 4. **Tests.** tests/browser/verify.e2e.test.ts covers both cases. 'a missing reference sample fails' empties the registry. It asserts a non-zero code, 'FAIL verify [sample]', the 'is not registered' message, and that no preview starts. 'an out-of-order sample fails naming the step' asserts a sample-phase failure at step 1 (index 0). The dissent (an emptied step list surfacing only as a render timeout) relies on a partial-deletion scenario. The guidance says not to construct those, and the candidate does not produce it. The guidance also says a dedicated regression test is not needed when the check is explicit, and here there are both explicit checks and tests.

first_results.rationale: Only one delivered test drives a browser directly: 'captures only after the transition settles' in tests/browser/inspect.int.test.ts. It launches chromium and calls page.setContent and page.evaluate. Inside the page it awaits img.decode() before reading pixels. Each of these awaited calls resolves only once its state is ready. There is no waitForTimeout, sleep, or count-read used as if it waited. The other browser tests (tests/browser/verify.e2e.test.ts and tests/browser/bootstrap.int.test.ts) run npm scripts through runNpm. runNpm resolves on the child's 'close' event (tests/browser/helpers.ts:52-64), so their assertions run on the finished process output. Its setTimeout is a kill timeout, not a wait before an assertion. previewIsGone does a fetch with a timeout, not a sleep. Judge C points to page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) in the inspect run loop. That call is in scripts/lib/inspect-run.mjs:50, the inspect helper's own settle delay, not in any test. The integration test checks the helper's output files; it does not sleep itself. The criterion asks whether the tests wait on state, and the review guidance lists longer fixed settle delays as validator noise. So C's observation does not make the test requirement fail. Judges A and B are correct that no browser test sleeps for a fixed time.

results.rationale: The suite that drives a browser is set in vitest.browser.config.ts (include 'tests/browser/**/*.test.ts'). That glob matches exactly three files: inspect.int.test.ts, verify.e2e.test.ts and bootstrap.int.test.ts. helpers.ts is their shared module. The unit config runs tests/unit under jsdom and does not drive a real browser. I quote all four browser files in full, and none of them sleeps for a fixed time or uses an immediately-returning call as a wait. (1) inspect.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits runNpm subprocess runs. The only direct Playwright test, 'captures only after the transition settles', awaits chromium.launch, page.setContent and page.evaluate, and the evaluate awaits img.decode(). It then asserts on pixel counts that have already been computed. The remaining tests assert on PNG files and output that the completed runs produced. (2) verify.e2e.test.ts: every test awaits runNpm and then asserts on the finished process's output and exit code. previewIsGone is a fetch bounded by AbortSignal.timeout. The only setTimeout in the file is in-page app code that a fault case injects into Scene.tsx. (3) bootstrap.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits spawnSync and runNpm, and the tests assert on their results and on file contents. (4) helpers.ts: runNpm resolves on the child's 'close' event. Its setTimeout is only a SIGKILL safeguard for a hung child, not a wait before an assertion. Inside the scripts, step changes are awaited by polling: waitForStepIndex calls page.waitForFunction on data-step-index with a timeout. Judge C's fail rests on page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) at scripts/lib/inspect-run.mjs:50. That call is in the delivered inspect helper, not in a test. The helper reaches it only after waitForStepIndex has confirmed the step (line 45), so the test's step assertions are not waiting on a sleep. The settle delay is a product option (--settle-ms) that the test exercises: it compares default-delay captures with --settle-ms 0 captures. The test does not use it to time its own assertions. The criterion is about how the browser tests wait, and the guidance excludes settle-delay length from scoring. Judge C's reason therefore does not decide the requirement, and I agree with Judges A and B.

- Ruling: This is partly a sample defect, which I fixed, and partly inherent to the approved design, which I did not change.

"text": "## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Interactive requirement gathering
The skill SHALL gather presentation details by asking the user clarifying questions one at a time — covering the topic, the visual style, and the content and visual description of each step. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.

#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details
- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions
- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it

#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail
- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details
- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate

#### Scenario: Prompt already complete
- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details
- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions

#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step
- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex
- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step

### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold
Before creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:

1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.
2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.
3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.

Detection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.

The scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.

The skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.

#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory
- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present
- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation

#### Scenario: Already scaffolded
- **WHEN** all three anchors are already present
- **THEN** the skill skips scaffolding and proceeds directly to creating or modifying the presentation

#### Scenario: Partial scaffold
- **WHEN** some but not all anchors are present
- **THEN** the skill scaffolds only the missing anchors (and their dependencies) without disturbing the ones already present

#### Scenario: Scaffold does not impose a style system
- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds a presentation app
- **THEN** the generated app can build without Tailwind or another styling framework
- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens

#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory
- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates
- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's own `SKILL.md` directory

#### Scenario: Monorepo target
- **WHEN** the skill runs inside a monorepo
- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app into a `presentations/` directory as its own self-contained app rather than at the repository root

#### Scenario: Standalone project target
- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds in an empty or standalone (non-monorepo) project
- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app at the repository root

#### Scenario: Non-empty project missing scaffolding
- **WHEN** the project is non-empty but lacks the scene kit or presentation index
- **THEN** the skill states the target location it will scaffold into and proceeds only after the user confirms

### Requirement: Create a new presentation
The skill SHALL generate a new presentation as a self-contained unit reachable at its own route and registered so that multiple presentations coexist.

#### Scenario: New presentation is self-contained and routed
- **WHEN** a new presentation is created
- **THEN** it is written as its own folder, reachable at its own route, and registered in the presentation index

#### Scenario: Presentation owns its visual style
- **WHEN** the skill creates a presentation with a designed visual look
- **THEN** the styling is added in files owned by that presentation or by the host app rather than in the reusable scene kit
- **AND** plain CSS is the default styling approach unless the host project already uses a styling framework or the user explicitly requests one

#### Scenario: Existing presentations are preserved
- **WHEN** a new presentation is created and other presentations already exist
- **THEN** the existing presentations remain intact and reachable

### Requirement: Modify an existing presentation
The skill SHALL support modifying an existing presentation, identifying the target first and asking only about the requested changes.

#### Scenario: Target unspecified or ambiguous
- **WHEN** the skill is asked to modify a presentation without a clear target
- **THEN** it lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything

#### Scenario: Scoped modification
- **WHEN** the target presentation is identified
- **THEN** the skill asks only about the requested changes (steps, entities, or style) and edits that presentation without re-walking the full create flow

### Requirement: Self-verify before reporting completion
Before reporting success, the skill SHALL confirm that the generated or modified presentation builds, renders without errors, and is visually coherent in a browser, fixing any failures itself. The render check SHALL at minimum render the presentation's first step without runtime or console errors; the full multi-step render check across every step is defined by the `presentation-verification` capability. The visual composition check SHALL inspect screenshots or an equivalent browser view of the first step, the last step, and any dense/key steps; responsive-sensitive presentations SHALL also be checked at a narrow viewport. When a project-local screenshot helper is available, the skill SHALL prefer it over ad hoc scripts outside the project tree so browser tooling resolves from local dependencies, settled screenshots are captured after animations complete, and advisory visual warnings can be reviewed.

#### Scenario: Checks run before done
- **WHEN** the skill finishes generating or modifying a presentation
- **THEN** it runs the build, at least a first-step render check, and a browser visual composition check before reporting completion

#### Scenario: Failures are fixed, not reported as success
- **WHEN** the build, render, or visual composition check fails
- **THEN** the skill fixes the issues and re-checks rather than reporting success

### Requirement: Generated presentation quality bar
Every generated presentation SHALL build with no type errors, render its first step without runtime errors, present a caption per step, support next/previous navigation, pass a visual composition check, and conform to the evolving-scene model.

#### Scenario: Builds clean
- **WHEN** a presentation is generated
- **THEN** `npm run build` completes with no type errors

#### Scenario: Renders without errors
- **WHEN** the presentation route is opened
- **THEN** it renders its first step with no runtime or console errors

#### Scenario: Captions and navigation present
- **WHEN** viewing a presentation
- **THEN** each step shows a caption and the user can navigate to the next and previous steps

#### Scenario: Visual composition is inspected
- **WHEN** a presentation is generated or modified
- **THEN** key browser screenshots or equivalent browser views show that important scene content fits the fixed canvas, intentional overlaps remain readable, and content does not collide with chrome such as captions, progress indicators, table of contents, or navigation controls

#### Scenario: Screenshot helper is project-local
- **WHEN** the skill captures screenshots for visual inspection
- **THEN** it uses the scaffolded project-local helper when available, or otherwise writes any temporary Playwright helper under the project root

#### Scenario: Visual warnings are reviewed
- **WHEN** the screenshot helper emits overlap or chrome-polish warnings
- **THEN** the skill reviews the referenced steps, fixes accidental collisions or indistinct current-step chrome, and marks only intentional readable overlaps as allowed

#### Scenario: Active chrome and attribution are styled locally
- **WHEN** the generated presentation includes table-of-contents, progress, navigation, or attribution chrome
- **THEN** presentation-owned or host-owned CSS makes the active step visibly distinct and the attribution legible
- **AND** the reusable scene kit remains free of default colors, fonts, borders, button styles, and theme tokens

## Where is the GitHub URL for the attribution link?
- Requirement: "Kit attribution" says the link reads "made by and-scene" and points to "the and-scene GitHub repository" but gives no URL.
- Ruling: The URL is `https://github.com/Codagent-AI/and-scene`, the repository's `origin` remote. It is one exported constant in the kit, and the attribution accepts an override prop.
- Rationale: It is the only and-scene repository the project knows of. A constant keeps it testable by unit test.
- Pending decision: None. If the canonical public URL differs, the user changes one constant.
## Does `MIN_SCALE` ever override a valid positive fit? (supersedes the scaling ruling's floor, clipping, and 320 px limit)

- Requirement: evolving-scene-presentations, "Fixed-canvas fit scaling" (the diagram is "scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport"; "Uniform scaling on resize"; per-mode fit geometry). Design, "Stage" (scale is "constant within a mode"; "scaled by `useFitScale` to the gap between header and footer"). Design's file layout lists a `MIN_SCALE` constant with no value or semantics. Neither document gives a minimum supported width or allows clipping at a valid viewport.
- Ruling: The earlier scaling ruling went beyond the approved text in two places, and this ruling replaces them.
- Replaced: "`MIN_SCALE` is used and the stage clips" when the raw fit is below it, and "320 × 568 is the narrowest supported width".

- For every finite, positive available width and height, in either mode, the scale is exactly the raw fit, `min(availW/DESIGN_W, availH/DESIGN_H)` on that mode's `STAGE_LAYOUT` geometry. This holds even when the result is below `MIN_SCALE`.

- `MIN_SCALE` is a fallback used only when the measurement is degenerate (zero, negative, or non-finite available width or height, for example before first layout). It is not a lower clamp, so there is no `max(fit, MIN_SCALE)`.
- Scale stays identical across steps at a fixed viewport and mode. It is recalculated on viewport resize and on mode change, and internal canvas coordinates never change.
- The checks are unit and component tests:
- raw fit is returned exactly at representative viewports, including 320 × 568 and a tiny viewport well below any real device (for example 40 × 40, where the fit is under `MIN_SCALE`);
- scale is equal across steps and changes on resize and on mode change;
- inspection that the transform is a single uniform scale.
- 320 × 568 is a representative fixture only. It is not a supported-width limit and adds no scope.

- Rationale: A clamp that engages at a valid positive viewport would let the diagram exceed the available space, which contradicts the spec's "fit". The approved text has nothing that permits clipping, and `MIN_SCALE` has no stated semantics, so the narrowest reading consistent with the spec is a degenerate-measurement fallback.
- Pending decision: None. No approved requirement changes.

"text": "## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Interactive requirement gathering
The skill SHALL gather presentation details by asking the user clarifying questions one at a time — covering the topic, the visual style, and the content and visual description of each step. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.

#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details
- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions
- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it

#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail
- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details
- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate

#### Scenario: Prompt already complete
- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details
- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions

#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step
- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex
- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step

### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold
Before creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:

1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.
2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.
3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.

Detection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.

The scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.

The skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.

#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory
- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present
- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation

#### Scenario: Already scaffolded
- **WHEN** all three anchors are already present
- **THEN** the skill skips scaffolding and proceeds directly to creating or modifying the presentation

#### Scenario: Partial scaffold
- **WHEN** some but not all anchors are present
- **THEN** the skill scaffolds only the missing anchors (and their dependencies) without disturbing the ones already present

#### Scenario: Scaffold does not impose a style system
- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds a presentation app
- **THEN** the generated app can build without Tailwind or another styling framework
- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens

#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory
- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates
- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's own `SKILL.md` directory

#### Scenario: Monorepo target
- **WHEN** the skill runs inside a monorepo
- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app into a `presentations/` directory as its own self-contained app rather than at the repository root

#### Scenario: Standalone project target
- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds in an empty or standalone (non-monorepo) project
- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app at the repository root

#### Scenario: Non-empty project missing scaffolding
- **WHEN** the project is non-empty but lacks the scene kit or presentation index
- **THEN** the skill states the target location it will scaffold into and proceeds only after the user confirms

### Requirement: Create a new presentation
The skill SHALL generate a new presentation as a self-contained unit reachable at its own route and registered so that multiple presentations coexist.

#### Scenario: New presentation is self-contained and routed
- **WHEN** a new presentation is created
- **THEN** it is written as its own folder, reachable at its own route, and registered in the presentation index

#### Scenario: Presentation owns its visual style
- **WHEN** the skill creates a presentation with a designed visual look
- **THEN** the styling is added in files owned by that presentation or by the host app rather than in the reusable scene kit
- **AND** plain CSS is the default styling approach unless the host project already uses a styling framework or the user explicitly requests one

#### Scenario: Existing presentations are preserved
- **WHEN** a new presentation is created and other presentations already exist
- **THEN** the existing presentations remain intact and reachable

### Requirement: Modify an existing presentation
The skill SHALL support modifying an existing presentation, identifying the target first and asking only about the requested changes.

#### Scenario: Target unspecified or ambiguous
- **WHEN** the skill is asked to modify a presentation without a clear target
- **THEN** it lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything

#### Scenario: Scoped modification
- **WHEN** the target presentation is identified
- **THEN** the skill asks only about the requested changes (steps, entities, or style) and edits that presentation without re-walking the full create flow

### Requirement: Self-verify before reporting completion
Before reporting success, the skill SHALL confirm that the generated or modified presentation builds, renders without errors, and is visually coherent in a browser, fixing any failures itself. The render check SHALL at minimum render the presentation's first step without runtime or console errors; the full multi-step render check across every step is defined by the `presentation-verification` capability. The visual composition check SHALL inspect screenshots or an equivalent browser view of the first step, the last step, and any dense/key steps; responsive-sensitive presentations SHALL also be checked at a narrow viewport. When a project-local screenshot helper is available, the skill SHALL prefer it over ad hoc scripts outside the project tree so browser tooling resolves from local dependencies, settled screenshots are captured after animations complete, and advisory visual warnings can be reviewed.

#### Scenario: Checks run before done
- **WHEN** the skill finishes generating or modifying a presentation
- **THEN** it runs the build, at least a first-step render check, and a browser visual composition check before reporting completion

#### Scenario: Failures are fixed, not reported as success
- **WHEN** the build, render, or visual composition check fails
- **THEN** the skill fixes the issues and re-checks rather than reporting success

### Requirement: Generated presentation quality bar
Every generated presentation SHALL build with no type errors, render its first step without runtime errors, present a caption per step, support next/previous navigation, pass a visual composition check, and conform to the evolving-scene model.

#### Scenario: Builds clean
- **WHEN** a presentation is generated
- **THEN** `npm run build` completes with no type errors

#### Scenario: Renders without errors
- **WHEN** the presentation route is opened
- **THEN** it renders its first step with no runtime or console errors

#### Scenario: Captions and navigation present
- **WHEN** viewing a presentation
- **THEN** each step shows a caption and the user can navigate to the next and previous steps

#### Scenario: Visual composition is inspected
- **WHEN** a presentation is generated or modified
- **THEN** key browser screenshots or equivalent browser views show that important scene content fits the fixed canvas, intentional overlaps remain readable, and content does not collide with chrome such as captions, progress indicators, table of contents, or navigation controls

#### Scenario: Screenshot helper is project-local
- **WHEN** the skill captures screenshots for visual inspection
- **THEN** it uses the scaffolded project-local helper when available, or otherwise writes any temporary Playwright helper under the project root

#### Scenario: Visual warnings are reviewed
- **WHEN** the screenshot helper emits overlap or chrome-polish warnings
- **THEN** the skill reviews the referenced steps, fixes accidental collisions or indistinct current-step chrome, and marks only intentional readable overlaps as allowed

#### Scenario: Active chrome and attribution are styled locally
- **WHEN** the generated presentation includes table-of-contents, progress, navigation, or attribution chrome
- **THEN** presentation-owned or host-owned CSS makes the active step visibly distinct and the attribution legible
- **AND** the reusable scene kit remains free of default colors, fonts, borders, button styles, and theme tokens
"

## Where is the GitHub URL for the attribution link?
- Requirement: "Kit attribution" says the link reads "made by and-scene" and points to "the and-scene GitHub repository" but gives no URL.
- Ruling: The URL is `https://github.com/Codagent-AI/and-scene`, the repository's `origin` remote. It is one exported constant in the kit, and the attribution accepts an override prop.

## Does `MIN_SCALE` ever override a valid positive fit? (supersedes the scaling ruling's floor, clipping, and 320 px limit)

- Requirement: evolving-scene-presentations, "Fixed-canvas fit scaling" (the diagram is "scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport"; "Uniform scaling on resize"; per-mode fit geometry). Design, "Stage" (scale is "constant within a mode"; "scaled by `useFitScale` to the gap between header and footer"). Design's file layout lists a `MIN_SCALE` constant with no value or semantics. Neither document gives a minimum supported width or allows clipping at a valid viewport.
- Ruling: The earlier scaling ruling went beyond the approved text in two places, and this ruling replaces them.
- Replaced: "`MIN_SCALE` is used and the stage clips" when the raw fit is below it, and "320 × 568 is the narrowest supported width".

- For every finite, positive available width and height, in either mode, the scale is exactly the raw fit, `min(availW/DESIGN_W, availH/DESIGN_H)` on that mode's `STAGE_LAYOUT` geometry. This holds even when the result is below `MIN_SCALE`.

- `MIN_SCALE` is a fallback used only when the measurement is degenerate (zero, negative, or non-finite available width or height, for example before first layout). It is not a lower clamp, so there is no `max(fit, MIN_SCALE)`.
- Scale stays identical across steps at a fixed viewport and mode. It is recalculated on viewport resize and on mode change, and internal canvas coordinates never change.
- The checks are unit and component tests:
- raw fit is returned exactly at representative viewports, including 320 × 568 and a tiny viewport well below any real device (for example 40 × 40, where the fit is under `MIN_SCALE`);
- scale is equal across steps and changes on resize and on mode change;
- inspection that the transform is a single uniform scale.
- 320 × 568 is a representative fixture only. It is not a supported-width limit and adds no scope.

- Rationale: A clamp that engages at a valid positive viewport would let the diagram exceed the available space, which contradicts the spec's "fit". The approved text has nothing that permits clipping, and `MIN_SCALE` has no stated semantics, so the narrowest reading consistent with the spec is a degenerate-measurement fallback.
- Pending decision: None. No approved requirement changes.

AT-003 asks the tester to inspect entering and departing entities while traversing the committed nine-step reference scene. When an existing package.json is present, `plan.addDependencies` etc. are merged, but the lockfile is never copied or updated, and `npm install` in the CLI runs unconstrained. Separately, in the `plan.createPackage` branch, `name: path.basename(resolved.target)` can produce an invalid npm package name (e.g. uppercase or spaces in the directory name), which makes `npm install`/`npm ci` fail with an unclear error after files were already written.
  ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib/preview.mjs:121 In startPreview, when the child process exits early the loop throws PhaseError without anything else needed, but if `fetch` hangs (no timeout), the 30s deadline check is never reached because the await never resolves. A port accepted by another process that never responds stalls verify/inspect indefinitely, and on that path the preview child is never stopped by startPreview (callers only get `preview` after it returns).
  ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib/inspect-run.mjs:23 `readRegistry(root)` is called with a regex-based parser and the slug is then interpolated into the URL. More importantly, `waitForStepIndex(page, index)` is awaited with default 5s timeout and failures propagate as a generic Playwright timeout message, without naming the step; the inspect run also never attaches console/pageerror listeners, so a presentation that crashes mid-way yields only a timeout error and the already-captured screenshots give no hint.
